title: Verifiable delegation result
description: The output schema for every Verifiable Task Kind - Implementation, Repro, Migration. Its Result is a diff in a Workspace accompanied by a mechanical pass/fail signal the Worker produced itself. The Worker runs the command and iterates against it; the Runner never re-runs it, so what is here is the whole of the evidence that the change works.

summary.description: Two or three sentences: what was asked for, what you changed to get it, and anything about the approach a reader of the diff would otherwise have to infer. Not a restatement of the file list.

branch.description: The branch the work is on, as `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` reports it in the Workspace you were given. You did not choose it and must not change it.

files_changed.description: Every path you created, modified or deleted, repository-relative. An empty array says you changed nothing, which is a legitimate Result only when the request turned out to need no change - and then the summary has to say why.

diff_stat.description: The size of the change, as `git diff --stat` counts it.

files.description: How many files the diff touches.

verification.description: The Verification Signal: the command you ran to establish that the change works, and what it did. It is evidence and not authority - a passing signal never on its own licenses landing the change - so it has to name a command a reader can run again.

command.description: The command as you ran it, verbatim and complete, so that the reader can run the same one. Never a description of it.

exit_code.description: The exit code that command last produced, reported honestly. A non-zero code with `passed` true is only correct where the Task Kind inverts the signal.

passed.description: Whether the signal is the one this task requires. For Implementation and Migration that means the command succeeded. For Repro it is inverted: the test is correct precisely when it fails, so a passing test means the test is wrong - never that the code needs changing.

caveats.description: What a reader has to know before landing this: what you could not verify, what you guessed at, what you left undone, and anything the Verification Signal does not cover. Empty when there is genuinely nothing - but silence here is read as a claim that the change is complete.

expected_failure.description: Repro only: true when the Verification Signal is inverted, so that the command failing is the success condition. Null for every other Task Kind.
